Find the right tool. Skip the trial and error.

Every DIY mechanic has bought the wrong tool once. We are here to make sure it does not happen twice. Side-by-side comparisons of the tools that matter for home car repair, plus honest guides from someone who learned the hard way.

Compare Tools

OBD2 Scanners

Diagnose engine codes, read live data, and reset check engine lights. From basic code readers to professional bi-directional tools.

Floor Jacks

Lift your car safely for oil changes, brake jobs, and undercarriage work. From compact to heavy-duty.

Socket Sets

The foundation of any toolbox. From basic kits to master mechanic sets.

Torque Wrenches

Precision tightening that matters. From beam-style classics to digital wrenches for critical fasteners.

Jump Starters

Portable power for dead batteries. Compact lithium units that start cars, trucks, and charge your devices.

Impact Wrenches

Remove stubborn bolts and lug nuts with ease. From cordless to pneumatic.

Ratchet Sets

The tool you reach for most. From compact 1/4 drive to heavy-duty 1/2 inch.

Breaker Bars

The bar you grab when a bolt will not move. Longer handle, solid steel, no moving parts. The tool you grab when a ratchet won't budge it.

Jack Stands

Hold your car up safely while you work underneath. From budget ratcheting pairs to pro pin-style stands for trucks and SUVs.

Car Ramps

Drive up, get under, change the oil. No pump, no stands, no deflate. A stable set of plastic or foam ramps beats a jack for most under-car jobs.

Work Lights

See what you are working on. From USB rechargeable under-hood bars to floodlights that light the whole garage. Brightness is only half the story.

Air Compressors

Air for pneumatic tools, tire top-offs, and the occasional die grinder. Quiet 10-gallon units for the garage to oil-lubed Big Bore tanks for constant-flow tools.

Multimeters

Find the short, the draw, and the dead battery. From a $16 auto-ranging meter that does the job to a True RMS meter for electronics work.

Battery Chargers

Charge a dead battery and keep a car alive through the winter. From $30 smart maintainers that float a battery for months to 100A engine-start units that crank a dead truck.

Oil Filter Wrenches

Get a stuck or rounded oil filter off without shredding the can or cussing at your car. Cap wrenches that grab the filter's flutes, pliers for tight bays, and the universal tools that fit everything but grip nothing.

Brake Caliper Tools

Get a brake caliper piston back so new pads fit. Floating front calipers push straight in, rear calipers with the parking brake inside have to be rotated. Push tools, wind-back kits, and the single-purpose spreaders for fixed multi-piston calipers.

Bolt Extractors

Get a rounded, stuck, or broken bolt out without drilling a hole you regret. Fluted extractor sockets hammer onto a rounded head and bite harder as you turn. Spiral extractors dig into a broken stud. From a $22 single grip to a $148 impact-rated pro kit.

Screwdriver Sets

Turn a screw without rounding the head. The tip has to match the recess, and Japanese cars use a JIS recess that a standard Phillips does not sit in properly. From a $25 Craftsman set for the trunk to the $139 Wiha extra heavy duty kit for daily work.

Impact Socket Sets

A chrome hand socket is not built to be hit. Impact sockets are tougher, thicker walled, and cut 6-point so the load lands on the flats instead of the corners. From a $20 metric starter set to the $180 deep set for axle nuts, here is what actually survives an impact wrench.
